mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen sharply for two consecutive weeks (-53.3 to -18.9), indicating a return of commuting activity that generates incidental retail trips on the way to/from work, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -53.3 at t-2w to -18.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days is not higher than prior 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trajectory for two more weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility crosses above -40 (percent change) on a weekly mean basis, it signals a meaningful restoration of public transport usage that enables non-essential shopping trips, causing RETAIL_REC to rise within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -40 for the first time in the snapshot window
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -46.9 at t-2w to -38.9 at t-0w, crossing -40
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the subsequent two weeks after TRANSIT first exceeds -40, or reverses downward while TRANSIT stays above -40.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT compounds to produce a larger rebound in RETAIL_REC than either series alone would predict, because commuting and transit use jointly re-enable discretionary retail visits along daily routes.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise week-on-week simultaneously for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved continuously from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth rate over next 4 weeks is no larger than what WORKPLACES alone would predict via its historical univariate relationship, indicating no synergistic effect.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility from 15.9 to 10.0 signals loosening of stay-at-home policy compliance or restrictions, which under a reopening regime translates into increased retail and recreation footfall over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls for two consecutive weeks after a prior rising trend
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 15.9 at t-1w to 10.0 at t-0w after rising from 6.7 to 15.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to decline, or RESIDENTIAL reverses upward while RETAIL_REC still rises, invalidating the inverse linkage.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp one-week drop in PARKS (-5.1 to -13.0) suggests outdoor leisure activity is being curtailed, likely by weather or crowding limits, causing displaced recreational demand to shift toward indoor retail and recreation venues within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -5.1 at t-1w to -13.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following a PARKS decline, indicating no substitution effect between outdoor and indoor activity categories.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has plateaued near 10-11 percent change for the last two weeks, indicating essential-goods demand has stabilized at a steady-state level; this stability implies no additional seasonal pressure is pushing RETAIL_REC beyond its current recovery trajectory, so its four-week growth rate will moderate rather than accelerate.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stable between 10.0 and 11.3 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth accelerates substantially over the next four weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining flat, contradicting the steady-state dampening assumption.

mechanism_narrative: A single-week jump in WORKPLACES exceeding 25 points (as observed from -48.6 to -18.9) signals a discrete policy-driven reopening announcement; such abrupt deregulation events are typically followed within one week by a surge in RETAIL_REC as consumers resume in-person shopping.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises more than 25 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES jumped from -48.6 at t-1w to -18.9 at t-0w, a 29.7 point rise
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week following a WORKPLACES jump exceeding 25 points, indicating the policy-shock mechanism does not transmit to retail behavior.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of falling RESIDENTIAL mobility and rising TRANSIT mobility jointly indicates reduced home-bound behavior paired with increased out-of-home mobility capacity, producing a compounded increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks beyond what either series predicts alone.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines while TRANSIT simultaneously rises for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 15.9 to 10.0 while TRANSIT rose from -46.1 to -38.9 over the same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's four-week growth is statistically indistinguishable from the additive sum of RESIDENTIAL-only and TRANSIT-only predicted effects, showing no interaction amplification.
